concept.title: The V&V Assistant chat
concept.shortdesc: The panel on the right is the V&V Assistant, which sees your current step and everything you've entered so far.

ul.li: Ask it anything — brainstorming personas, tightening a requirement, challenging your framing.

Its replies can include suggestion cards (persona, need, requirement, NFR, hazard, or framing text). Click a card's add button to insert it into the wizard — replacement suggestions update an existing entry in place. Entries already materialized as artifacts can't be replaced from chat.
Quick actions (like Review step) send canned prompts, e.g. a quality-check of the current step's entries for clarity and testability.
The assistant is nudged automatically when you advance or skip a step, so it follows along with context.

section.title: The V&V Assistant on every page
section.p: The same assistant is on every project page and on the workspace Home, behind the ✦ Assistant button in the bottom corner. It opens a chat panel over the page:

ul.li: One conversation per project. What you asked in the wizard is there on every page and the other way round, and the panel keeps the conversation open while you move between pages. On the workspace Home, choose the project at the top of the panel.

Looking at: under the title says what the assistant is told you are reading: the requirement open in the Requirements page (it reads the whole artifact), or the page you are on. ✕ stops sending it, until you open something else.

⤢ expands the panel, ⇆ moves it to the other corner when it covers something you need, and dragging its top corner resizes it. — or Esc minimises it back to the button, and the conversation is still there when you open it again.
Alt+A (Option+A on a Mac) opens the panel and puts the cursor in the message box.
On a phone it opens as a sheet from the bottom of the screen.
The quick actions fit where you are: Review this and How would I verify it? beside a requirement, Gap analysis and Draft tests for the project as a whole.

section.p: Suggestion cards beside the project add a draft artifact, or make the change they describe, when you press their button, and only then. Ask for any change you could make yourself and the assistant answers with a card for it:

ul.li: Release: add a target release, or change one's name, date or status.
Release target: put artifacts in a release, optionally until a later one, or clear their own targeting so they follow their parent's.
Link: add a traceability link, remove one, or confirm a suspect link.
Review status: move artifacts to draft, in review, approved or superseded. A change the review workflow does not allow is refused on the card, with the reason.
Archive: archive artifacts, which keeps their history so they can be reinstated. Apply all never includes an archive card; each one is applied by its own button.
Comment: post a comment on an artifact, in your name.
To-do and Board task: raise a to-do or add a task to the board, assigned to a member and with a due date if the card names them.
Baseline, Review round and Test run: capture a baseline, send every draft for review, or record a test run's results.

section.p: Each card does what the same action on its page would, with your access: a change you could not make there is refused on the card too. Project settings, members, uploads and evidence files stay on their own pages. Other pages can start a turn for you: Draft tests on the V&V dashboard's Top gaps card opens the panel and asks for test cases for those gaps (see V&V → Gaps).
Starting a conversation needs editor access to the project, and a workspace its plan has made read-only cannot start one. In either case the panel says so and what to do instead of a chat.
On a workspace still on an earlier release, the assistant is a tab of the Notes panel on the Requirements page instead, beside the artifact's History.

Assistant turns execute on an agent runner like any other agent work. If no runner is online the panel says so and pauses replies — messages you send are saved and answered as soon as a runner connects (see Runs & runners).
